subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: Which QQBot identity must be allowed to resolve an implicit approval button in a direct C2C conversation when the bot accepts open or wildcard DMs?
rationale: The reported workflow needs a usable direct-chat approval path, but C2C privacy does not establish operator identity; choosing between request-bound recipient identity, explicit approvers, owner identity, or command authorization defines a security and product contract.

options.title: Bind to intended recipient
options.body: Carry the approval request's intended QQBot recipient identity into callback authorization and allow only that matching actor, preserving open chat without granting general approval authority.

options.title: Require explicit approver config
options.body: Keep current fail-closed behavior and require a concrete allowFrom or execApprovals.approvers entry, with clearer setup guidance for affected users.

options.title: Treat every C2C sender as trusted
options.body: Accept the PR's unconditional direct-chat bypass, intentionally allowing any open-DM sender to approve requests presented in their conversation.

recommendation.title: Bind to intended recipient
recommendation.body: Carry the approval request's intended QQBot recipient identity into callback authorization and allow only that matching actor, preserving open chat without granting general approval authority.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter most recently defined, proved, and merged the QQBot fallback approval authorization boundary and is the strongest history-based owner for this security choice.
